out.other_title: Open questions: scaling PVGs to harder problems and behaviour at approximate equilibria
out.rationale: Anil et al. call for scaling PVGs to more challenging problems. Hammond and Adam-Day report that on APPS code validation every protocol modestly beats a verifier trained alone, with nip and mnip gaining about 11% and mnip best on worst-case performance; training is eight rounds of expert iteration rather than equilibrium-seeking methods.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether prover-verifier protocols help weak verifiers on a realistic task, for GPT-4o provers and GPT-4o-mini verifiers on APPS code validation

text: On code validation the paper reports a modest improvement in final test accuracy over a verifier trained in isolation for every protocol tested, with nip and mnip giving the largest gains (around 11%). On worst-case performance, measured as the share of test points where the verifier is wrong in all 10 sampled rollouts, most protocols do significantly better than the solo verifier, with mnip best.
title: Code validation: all protocols modestly beat a solo verifier; nip and mnip gain about 11%
